priority.override_reason: Ranks 1 through 4 are closed by current direct-leaf frame-stack, constructor-leaf, and own-slot cache evidence. The fresh rank-5 profile shows a distinct remaining cost after the existing direct-eval blueprint cache: every cache hit still materializes and writes back the whole caller frame, although the reusable bytecode statically identifies its referenced and written names. The proposed guard is bytecode- and environment-shape-based only; it never selects a source path, benchmark name, checksum, or iteration count.

mechanism.summary: For a cache-hit direct eval whose reusable bytecode has no declarations, nested eval, or with scope, materialize only the caller bindings named by that bytecode plus the fixed call-context bindings instead of snapshotting every active caller slot.
mechanism.generality: Eligibility is derived from the existing direct-eval cache entry, immutable bytecode name sets, and the caller's dynamic-scope state. It applies to every matching direct eval regardless of source path or benchmark. Cache misses, declaration-bearing evals, nested eval, with, existing deoptimized bindings, and any unsupported call context retain the current complete frame snapshot and writeback path.
semantic_risks: a sparse frame must preserve lexical shadowing, TDZ values, captured-cell identity, and exact writes for every statically referenced or written binding
this, arguments, new.target, home object, super constructor, private environment, strictness, and parameter-scope metadata must remain available whenever the eval bytecode can observe them
a caller with existing dynamic bindings or with scope must decline before any partial environment is created
the fallback must remain byte-for-byte the current full direct-eval environment path for cache misses and unsupported source shapes

profile_evidence.shared_cost: The repeated cache-hit direct eval path enters native_global_eval but still reaches frame_call_env and apply_env. In 3,600 sampled main-thread stacks, apply_env has 165 top-of-stack samples, while the same paths show FrameBindings insertion, String cloning, hashing, memcmp, allocation, and free work from complete caller-frame materialization and writeback.
